cohort: Pregnant women from the Healthcare-Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) from 2010 to 2014 (3,846,342 births, with 6,195 deliveries to women with bicornuate uterus)
finding: Pregnant women with bicornuate uteri have significantly increased risks of various pregnancy complications, including premature delivery, cesarean delivery, PPROM, placental abruption, hysterectomy, SGA, and IUFD.
mod_finding: Women with bicornuate uteri were more likely to deliver preterm and by cesarean delivery.
